core_obligations: Turn torsion freeness of M over R into the injectivity of M to M tensor K, with K the fraction field of R (proof lines 4830-4831).
Apply flatness of R to R' to the injection of the previous step and obtain an injection M tensor R' to (M tensor K) tensor R' (proof lines 4832-4833).

Reduce the problem to the case of the fraction field by identifying M tensor K as a direct sum of copies of K, so that it suffices to know that K tensor R' is torsion free over R' (proof lines 4834-4835).
Conclude that K tensor R' is torsion free because it is a localisation of R' (proof lines 4835-4836).
proof_roadmap: Interval comparison against the 57 public records of more-algebra.tex: no recorded interval covers the counted statement 4824-4837, and the nearest records are 336 (4721-4764, tag 0H7R, descent of projectivity through finite injective ring extensions) and 335 (3382-3437, tag 09ZL, finite etale algebras over a henselian pair), neither of which is a torsion-freeness-under-base-change statement.
difficulty_reason: The statement is a base-change statement for torsion freeness along a flat map of domains, and the proof is a chain of three reductions that all have to be made in the correct order (statement lines 4824-4827, proof lines 4830-4837). One first sees that a torsion free M sits inside M tensor K and that flatness of R' over R keeps this injection after tensoring with R' (proof lines 4830-4833); the module M tensor K is then identified as a direct sum of copies of the fraction field so the problem is pushed to the single case K tensor R' (proof line 4834-4835), which is settled by recognising that module as a localisation of R' (proof line 4835-4836). What is not routine is the reduction step itself: it uses flatness of the ring map, not of the module, and it uses that torsion freeness is tested elementwise, so a reader cannot replace it by the (false) statement that an arbitrary tensor product of torsion free modules is torsion free.
